A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Thermalizer study. The main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Kolmogorov flow and quasi-geostrophic turbulence, including rollout stability, kinetic-energy spectra, autocorrelation, and thermalization analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a diagnostic showing thermalization counts along existing trajectories.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the emulator architectures and losses, and the diffusion model with its noise-classifying head remain unchanged. The expanded threshold-selection description documents the existing procedure rather than introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate on the same Kolmogorov and two-layer quasi-geostrophic systems. The added diagnostic examines existing Kolmogorov trajectories without introducing another dataset, task, or test environment.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain numerical simulations and thermalized versus unthermalized U-Net and Dilated ResNet emulators. The newly cited diffusion papers are discussed as related work, not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: Existing data splits, model sizes, training budgets, benchmark metrics, rollout lengths, and selected thermalization thresholds are retained. Appendix C.3 explains the previously mentioned brute-force tuning; the new heatmap analyzes an existing rollout window rather than changing the underlying evaluation settings.

E4.justification: New Figure 13 examines when corrective denoising occurs across 40 Kolmogorov trajectories for each emulator, using steps 5000–5500. This adds a limited diagnostic of adaptive intervention; the predicted-noise plot and single-thermalization-step analyses already existed in v1.

E5.justification: The trajectory counts, averaging, and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged, with no added seed replication, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The four searches disclosed in Appendix C.3 refer to different flow/emulator combinations, not repeated statistical runs.

E6.justification: New Figure 13 reports per-timestep thermalization counts ranging from 0 to 16 and their variation along trajectories. Existing MSE curves, spectra, autocorrelation, and total thermalization-count results are retained, including the 100,000-step spectra in v1 Figure 7 and v2 Figure 6.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, equations, transport argument, and KL-contraction inequality remain unchanged. The added reference to Ho et al. for alpha and beta parameters supplies explanatory attribution without adding a derivation or formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract strengthens the claimed extension of stable prediction horizons from one order of magnitude to two. The central contribution remains unchanged, and both versions already claim arbitrarily long stabilization in the introduction and demonstrate 100,000-step rollouts in the conclusion.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds interpretation of the numerical-model noise predictions as a classifier sanity check and of the new heatmap as alternating periods of no correction and stronger intervention. The limitations concerning Gaussian perturbations, threshold tuning, and imperfect long-run energy spectra are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 newly discloses threshold-search bounds, 10,000-step trials, selection by kinetic-energy agreement, and separate tuning for four flow/emulator combinations. Appendix C.2 replaces a future code-release promise with a specific repository address; the selected thresholds and other implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 3 and the references add Shehata et al. (2025) on efficient diffusion sampling and Rühling Cachay et al. (2024) on climate emulation. These modestly extend the related-work discussion without changing the central positioning against existing stabilization approaches.

P1.justification: Appendix C is divided into Architecture, Optimization, and Thermalizer settings subsections, and Appendix E gains explanatory paragraphs. There are limited wording and front-matter edits, while most prose and the overall section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 adds pink shading and a caption explanation for stable but decorrelated states. The marginal-distribution schematic moves from v1 Figure 5 to appendix Figure 11, a new thermalization-count heatmap becomes Figure 13, and existing figures are reflowed and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The clearer tuning recipe, explicit code-access information, and added intervention diagnostic modestly improve reproducibility and interpretability. Core experimental evidence and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged. The stronger abstract claim does not establish improved performance over v1, since the long-horizon results were already present.
